solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Beat or scolded delicate flower

blocks.note: to slipper someone is to beat them with a slipper
an old past tense of chide

explanation.surface: Someone thrashed and told off a fragile bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beat or scolded' reads as a pair of alternatives, but 'or' is simply kept as letters between the two verbs.
explanation.definitionFit: The slipper orchid is a showy orchid with a pouched lip, prized and tricky to grow.

clue.text: Quit position over drink

blocks.note: a stand is a position taken
to down a drink is to swallow it

explanation.surface: Someone resigns their post and heads off for a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand down is to resign or withdraw from an office or post.

clue.text: Deadlock that is broken by politician with seat in Boston

indicators.note: something broken open has another thing pushed into its middle

explanation.surface: A political stalemate is ended by a congressman taking a seat in Boston.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seat in Boston' points to American English, where the word for the backside differs from British arse.
explanation.definitionFit: An impasse is a situation where no progress is possible, a stalemate.

clue.text: Introduction for building toy figures: first class

explanation.surface: An introductory guide to making toy figures, rated top class.
explanation.definitionFit: A prolegomenon is a preliminary discussion or preface; the plural is used for an introduction to a work.

clue.text: Run, seeing baby elephant’s finally gone rogue

indicators.note: the final letter of the word is gone, removed from its end

blocks.note: as in the sense of since or because
a young elephant is a calf

explanation.surface: A baby elephant runs off and turns into a rogue elephant.
explanation.definitionFit: A rascal is a scamp or mischievous rogue, someone of dishonest character.

clue.text: Minister’s front-page retreat after U-turn

indicators.note: a U-turn makes the word face back the other way

blocks.note: the recto is the right-hand, front side of a leaf

explanation.surface: A newspaper's front-page story on a minister's retreat after a policy U-turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Rectorial is the adjective of rector, a minister in charge of a parish, so it means belonging to such a cleric.

clue.text: Maybe one in the morning pile surrounding setter?

blocks.note: first meaning: a morning drink taken to ease a hangover
second meaning, whimsical: the pile, or coat, covering an Irish or English setter

explanation.walkthrough: The setter is not the crossword compiler but a breed of gun dog, whose coat or pile surrounds it.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names an alcoholic drink taken the morning after, supposedly to cure a hangover.

clue.text: Absorbing noise, muffling sound of bell when relatives visit

indicators.note: to muffle something is to wrap around it
visitors come in and stay inside the household

blocks.note: a din is a loud noise

explanation.surface: A noisy family gathering drowns out the doorbell as the relatives arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: Two insertions nest: the relatives go inside the bell's sound, and that sits inside the noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Drinking in a sight or sound means taking it in eagerly, absorbing it fully.

clue.text: Checks speed of fabulous runner-up in holiday location

blocks.note: to time a runner is to check their speed
in Aesop's fable the hare loses the race to the tortoise

explanation.surface: A coach clocks the second-placed runner at a holiday resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fabulous' means from a fable: the hare finished second to the tortoise.
explanation.definitionFit: A timeshare is a holiday property jointly owned, each owner using it for a set period.

clue.text: That is to say, nothing lost for a fool

indicators.note: what is lost is taken away from the phrase

blocks.note: to wit means namely, that is to say

explanation.surface: A wry aside: losing everything makes you look a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A twit is a silly or stupid person, an informal word for an idiot.

clue.text: Muslim ritual adapted to accommodate system of belief in toleration of diversity

indicators.note: adapted means changed in form, so the letters are rearranged
accommodating something means making room for it inside

blocks.note: a cult is a system of religious devotion

explanation.surface: A religious rite is modified to make room for other faiths in a tolerant society.
explanation.definitionFit: Multiculturalism is the policy of accepting and valuing many cultures within one society.

clue.text: Primarily street-based language

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter counts

explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines, and the wordplay is the initial of street with LANG, the dictionary abbreviation for language, set after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang is informal vocabulary, much of it born on the street rather than in formal speech.

clue.text: Interest rate: no choice but one, apparently, reasoned logically

blocks.note: a choice of one or one, written with the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A borrower finds only one interest rate on offer and reasons it through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One or one' is no real choice: written with Roman numerals it is I OR I.
explanation.definitionFit: A priori reasoning works from principles to conclusions, deduced logically rather than from experience.

clue.text: Treatment centre showing mercy with more gone, sadly

indicators.note: things that turn out sadly have gone wrong, so the letters come out in a bad order

explanation.surface: A hospital that has run out of compassion, more's the pity.
explanation.walkthrough: An emergency room is the American name for what Britons call A&E.
explanation.definitionFit: An emergency room is the hospital department giving urgent medical treatment to arrivals.

clue.text: Programme run out on this is awaiting confirmation

definitions.note: goods 'on appro' are awaiting confirmation of purchase

blocks.note: an app is a computer program
the cricket scorer's abbreviation for run out

explanation.surface: A broadcast schedule has overrun and is waiting to be signed off.
explanation.walkthrough: Appro is British shorthand for approval: goods sent on appro can be returned if the buyer does not confirm.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods supplied on approval may be kept or returned, so the sale awaits the customer's say-so.

clue.text: Concerned with offering of bones that’s accepted if here in Lourdes

indicators.note: what is accepted is taken in and held

blocks.note: relating to the sacrum, the bone at the base of the spine
French for here; Lourdes is in France

explanation.surface: At Lourdes, relics of a saint's bones are received as a pious offering.
explanation.walkthrough: SACRAL takes in IF and ICI, the French for here.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacrificial describes what relates to a sacrifice, an offering made to a deity.

clue.text: Enjoy view in common area gardened regularly

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is used

blocks.note: first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: Neighbours admire the outlook across a shared green that's tended at intervals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Enjoy' here means to have the benefit of, so to enjoy a view in common is to share an opinion.
explanation.definitionFit: To agree is to share the same opinion as someone else, holding a common position.

clue.text: Outlaw ropes dead bucks

indicators.note: a horse that bucks throws everything out of place

explanation.surface: A cowboy lassoes dead bucks, male deer, in a Wild West scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A desperado is a reckless criminal, especially a bandit of the American West.

clue.text: Firm with fine deferring 1,000

indicators.note: something deferred is put off till later, so it moves back in the word

explanation.surface: A company is fined but pays the thousand later.
explanation.walkthrough: The K for 1,000 in OKAY is moved one place later.
explanation.definitionFit: Oaky means hard or solid like oak timber, hence firm; it also describes wine tasting of oak.

clue.text: Daughters displacing sons in round-campfire activity perhaps causing argument

indicators.note: to displace something is to take its place

blocks.note: a group singing round a campfire
genealogical abbreviation, replacing each S for sons

explanation.surface: The girls push the boys out of the campfire circle, starting a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: A ding-dong is British slang for a heated row.
explanation.definitionFit: A ding-dong is informal British for a noisy quarrel, a heated argument.

clue.text: Got big house by delta

explanation.surface: Someone acquired a large house by a river delta.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Got' here means understood, as in 'I got it'.
explanation.definitionFit: To fathom something is to work out its meaning, to understand it fully.

clue.text: State‘s mineral aggregate almost exhausted

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the end is cut off

blocks.note: rock from which metal is mined

explanation.surface: A US state's mineral deposits are nearly worked out.
explanation.definitionFit: Oregon is a state in the Pacific Northwest of the United States.

clue.text: Ringing reporter, animated, criminal lain out after arrest

indicators.note: criminal means wrong or bent, so the letters are twisted
after places the shuffled words second, behind the word for arrest

explanation.surface: A cartoon reporter rings in a story of a criminal sprawled out after his arrest.
explanation.definitionFit: Tintinnabulation is the ringing or tinkling sound of bells.

clue.text: Reference work a sailor picked up

indicators.note: in a down answer, lifting the word up makes it read from bottom to top

blocks.note: an old salt is a seasoned sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor collects a book of maps from the library.
explanation.definitionFit: An atlas is a book of maps, a standard work of reference.

clue.text: Rating description of tablet by joint article

blocks.note: the word tablet has ABLE as its body, between the Ts

explanation.surface: A pharmacist's label describes a pill and how it treats an aching joint.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the outer Ts from tablet and its body is ABLE, so tablet is 'able-bodied'. A rating is a non-commissioned sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: An able seaman is a naval rating, a sailor of the lower deck with basic qualifications.

clue.text: At no point omitting English during poor delivery, clipped and inarticulate?

indicators.note: omitting means leaving something out
what happens during something lies within it
clipped means trimmed short at the end

blocks.note: an illegal ball bowled in cricket

explanation.surface: A tongue-tied speaker never quite manages to get the words out in English.
explanation.walkthrough: A no-ball is a cricket delivery that breaks the rules; shortened to NOBAL, it surrounds NEVER minus one E.
explanation.definitionFit: Non-verbal communication uses no words, so in a playful sense it is inarticulate; hence the question mark.

clue.text: What the virtuous have for starters

blocks.note: read as two words: what good people lack is any moral failing

explanation.surface: A question about what good people order as a first course.
explanation.walkthrough: The virtuous have NO VICES; run together, that spells beginners. 'Starters' looks like a first course of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Novices are beginners, people new to an activity or just starting out.

clue.text: Essence described by letter that backs description

indicators.note: to describe a circle is to draw round it, so one word goes inside another
a letter that backs runs backwards

blocks.note: the spelt name of the letter T
the pith is the core or essence

explanation.surface: The heart of a letter is the description it endorses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Described by' uses the geometric sense: a line describes a circle by drawing round it.
explanation.definitionFit: An epithet is a descriptive word or phrase attached to a name, a characterising description.

clue.text: Out of practice, but with change of hands becoming strong

indicators.note: the right hand is swapped for the left one

blocks.note: skills that are rusty are unpractised
L for left replaces R for right

explanation.surface: A rusty player swaps hands and finds strength.
explanation.definitionFit: Lusty means healthy and vigorous, full of strength and energy.

clue.text: Cloud of mounting suspicion enveloping prostitute

indicators.note: to envelop is to wrap something inside
in a down answer, mounting means rising, so the letters read upwards

blocks.note: British slang, as in arrested 'on sus'

explanation.surface: A cloud of growing suspicion hangs over a prostitute.
explanation.walkthrough: Sus is British slang for suspicion, as in the old police power to stop someone 'on sus'.
explanation.definitionFit: Stratus is a low, grey, layered cloud forming a uniform sheet across the sky.

clue.text: Grotto with gold holds a lure: take things at your own risk

definitions.text: take things at your own risk

indicators.note: to hold is to keep something inside

blocks.note: a grotto is a small cave

explanation.surface: Treasure in a cave draws in an adventurer, who must accept the danger.
explanation.walkthrough: CAVE plus OR holds A TEMPT: CAVE(A TEMPT)OR.
explanation.definitionFit: Caveat emptor is Latin for 'let the buyer beware': the purchaser bears the risk.

clue.text: Way to cut emissions from vehicle, fitting universal filter at back, held by nut

indicators.note: at the back means only the very last letter is used
what is held by something sits inside it

explanation.surface: A car's exhaust gets a universal filter to cut its pollution.
explanation.walkthrough: Bonce is British slang for the head, like nut; it holds APT, U and R after its first four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Carbon capture traps carbon dioxide from emissions before it reaches the atmosphere.

clue.text: Cook vegetable à la Spooner and thank the Lord

indicators.note: in the manner of Reverend Spooner, who swapped the opening sounds of words

blocks.note: to braise is to cook slowly; swap the opening sounds

explanation.surface: A grateful cook stews some greens and gives thanks to God.
explanation.definitionFit: Praise be is an exclamation of thanksgiving to God, expressing relief or gratitude.

clue.text: Paris and Rome arranged by international producer

indicators.note: arranged means put into a new order

blocks.note: the anagram fodder, the and being a joining word

explanation.surface: A world-touring showman puts on productions in Paris and Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: An impresario organises and finances concerts, plays or operas, a theatrical producer.

clue.text: Expose evidence, and prepare for storm

blocks.note: to weather something is to leave it exposed to the elements

explanation.surface: A detective reveals the evidence and readies for the furore.
explanation.definitionFit: To weatherproof a building is to make it resistant to rain and wind before bad weather arrives.

clue.text: A pro circle in which characters trade places with give and take

indicators.note: when the letters trade places, they end up in a different sequence

explanation.surface: Professional players form a circle and swap positions in a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Reciprocal arrangements are mutual, each side giving and receiving in equal measure.

clue.text: What‘s power line carrying electricity ultimately supported by?

definitions.text: What‘s power line carrying electricity ultimately supported by?

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only the last letter counts
to carry is to hold something within

blocks.note: resting on something means being supported by it; in a down answer it goes beneath

explanation.surface: A quiz question about what holds up the overhead cables of the electricity grid.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition, and the wordplay builds it: P and L carry the last letter of electricity, with ON below.
explanation.definitionFit: Overhead power lines are carried on pylons, the tall steel towers that hold up cables.

clue.text: Outdated hierarchy made less fusty, somehow, not having succeeded

indicators.note: somehow means by some unknown means, so the letters are reworked
not having something means it is left out

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned social order was modernised but didn't quite work.
explanation.definitionFit: The feudal system was the medieval social order of lords, vassals and serfs, long obsolete.

clue.text: Faint-hearted messengers in Book of Numbers?

explanation.surface: Cowardly messengers appear in the Old Testament's Book of Numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book of Numbers' looks biblical but means a book of telephone numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellow Pages is a classified telephone directory, a book listing business phone numbers.

clue.text: I’ll be bound by outrageous residence order

indicators.note: outrageous means wildly out of line, so the letters go wild
being bound by something means being tied up within it

explanation.surface: A prisoner is confined by a court ruling to an outrageous house.
explanation.walkthrough: Decree nisi is the provisional order in an English divorce.
explanation.definitionFit: A decree nisi is a court order that a divorce will become final unless cause is shown.

clue.text: Bird of river and lake

blocks.note: the Ouse is an English river

explanation.surface: A bird that lives by river and lake.
explanation.definitionFit: The ousel is an old name for the blackbird, or the related ring ouzel and water ouzel.

clue.text: Check pressure during cricket, say

indicators.note: what happens during something lies within it

blocks.note: the cricket is an example of an insect

explanation.surface: An umpire checks the pressure in the middle of a cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cricket' wants to be the game, but 'say' marks it as an example: an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspect is to examine something closely, to check it for faults.

clue.text: Storage facility misses leaks

blocks.note: to miss out on is to lose

explanation.surface: A warehouse lets stock go missing.
explanation.definitionFit: To disclose is to make known secret information, which is what leaking does.

clue.text: Severe daughter with tiny motor perhaps turning up to collect one

indicators.note: in a down answer, turning up makes the letters read upwards
collecting something means taking it in

blocks.note: the Tata Nano, a tiny Indian car

explanation.surface: A father is strict when his daughter's little car turns up to collect a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Draconian means excessively harsh, after Draco, the Athenian lawgiver whose laws were notoriously severe.

clue.text: Start of school perhaps hairy and tense

indicators.note: the start means just the opening letter

blocks.note: full of tresses, locks of hair; 'perhaps' flags an invented word

explanation.surface: A first day at school might feel scary and nerve-racking.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stressful causes strain and anxiety, making a person tense.

clue.text: Romantic writer‘s blue poem and wine capturing dearest’s heart

indicators.note: to capture is to take inside
the heart is the very middle letter

blocks.note: a wine from the Bergerac region of France

explanation.surface: A lovelorn poet writes a melancholy verse over wine, winning his sweetheart's heart.
explanation.walkthrough: Cyrano is famed as the big-nosed romantic hero of Rostand's play, who wooed for another man.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyrano de Bergerac was a 17th-century French author, immortalised as a romantic hero by Rostand.

clue.text: Blooming got up then had breakfast?

explanation.surface: A morning routine: rise and have breakfast.
explanation.definitionFit: Roseate means rosy, pink like a rose, hence of a fresh healthy blooming complexion.

clue.text: Football scout endlessly rings round

indicators.note: without an end, the final letter is dropped
turned round means facing the other way

blocks.note: rings shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A talent scout phones around about a promising footballer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scout' and 'rings' look like a talent spotter's phone calls; recce means a reconnaissance.
explanation.definitionFit: Soccer is association football, the name used especially in America.

clue.text: Tory record is to comply

blocks.note: a criminal's form is their record

explanation.surface: A Conservative's voting record is to toe the line.
explanation.walkthrough: Tory is the everyday name for a member of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: To conform is to behave according to rules or standards, to comply with them.

clue.text: Fur stole covered up boxes

indicators.note: the phrase boxes the word, holding it within
in a down answer, up means reading from bottom to top

blocks.note: the letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A fur stole is wrapped up in boxes for storage.
explanation.definitionFit: The ocelot is a spotted wild cat whose pelt was once prized as fur.

clue.text: Dealer secures old volume, customer offering little resistance

indicators.note: to secure something is to lock it safely inside

explanation.surface: A book dealer secures an antique volume from a customer who barely haggles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dealer' looks like a bookseller, but it is a drug pusher.
explanation.definitionFit: A pushover is someone easily persuaded or beaten, offering little resistance.

clue.text: Operation where one’s put under, I hesitate to say, getting drug

blocks.note: Roman numeral one, placed below in a down answer

explanation.surface: A patient is put under for an operation and, hesitantly, is given a narcotic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put under' sounds like anaesthesia but means placed below, in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Opium is a narcotic drug made from the dried latex of the opium poppy.

clue.text: Deputy backing grievance, mostly

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the end is cut off
backing means going backwards

explanation.surface: A deputy supports a complaint, for the most part.
explanation.walkthrough: Veep is American slang for vice-president.
explanation.definitionFit: Veep is an informal US term for a vice-president, the deputy to the president.

clue.text: Plaster over outside toilet with people inside?

indicators.note: turned over means flipped to read the other way
being outside something means wrapping round it

explanation.surface: A builder plasters over an outdoor loo with someone still in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Occupants are the people living in or occupying a building, the ones inside.

clue.text: Wander? Not right: don’t go!

indicators.note: not having something means it is removed

explanation.surface: A plea to someone about to wander off the right path: stay here.
explanation.definitionFit: Stay is the command to remain where you are, the opposite of leave.

clue.text: Extract of gum: a mild taste

indicators.note: an extract is a portion taken from within the text

blocks.note: the letters running across the words

explanation.surface: A gum extract with a gentle flavour.
explanation.definitionFit: Umami is the savoury fifth basic taste, alongside sweet, sour, salty and bitter.

clue.text: Old Chinese leader, out of condition, returned rested for wedding

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective: for a wedding

indicators.note: being out of something means sitting around its outside
returned means sent back, so read backwards

blocks.note: in good trim means in good condition

explanation.surface: A former Chinese leader, out of shape, comes back rested for a wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: Matrimonial means relating to marriage, so it suits a wedding.

clue.text: Act awkwardly with female then leave

explanation.surface: A woman embarrasses herself and makes her exit.
explanation.definitionFit: Go off is a phrasal verb for departing, as an actor exits the stage.

clue.text: A good chance of stable currency?

explanation.surface: An economist predicts a likely period of steady currency.
explanation.walkthrough: Even money is betting odds of one to one, a fifty-fifty chance.
explanation.definitionFit: Even money means odds of evens, so an outcome as likely as not: a fair chance.

clue.text: During Times final I solved very little

indicators.note: solved means worked out, so the letters are sorted into a new order

explanation.surface: A solver boasts of finishing very little in the Times crossword final.
explanation.definitionFit: Infinitesimal means extremely small, so tiny as to be almost immeasurable.
